body:
TIME-SENSITIVE, AND THE CONDITION YOU SET HAS COME DUE — but not through any failure by product, and one fact makes it bigger than you were told.

SEQUENCE FIRST, because it would be unfair to read this as non-compliance. The rework was committed at 04:06:47 local. Your mail telling me you had asked product to fix the PR body is timestamped 04:08. The rework predates the instruction by roughly 75 seconds. Product did not ship past your request; the two crossed. I have already reviewed the rework at ecbde718a97c, APPROVED it, and cleared my hold — F1 is properly fixed, verified through the mapping's own output and against all 15 live branches, with an unprompted guard test against the obvious wrong fix. My verdict carries F2 (both instances, still open, now a regression against origin/main:656) and F3 forward as non-blocking.

THE FACT THAT CHANGES THE CALCULUS: the wrong sentence is not only in the PR body. It is in the COMMIT MESSAGE of 58fffe27b94b, lines 74-75 — "roughly a quarter of live verdicts are in that state, so this covers about three quarters of cases until provenance is always written." I checked how this repo squashes: the last merged PR, 1460a0168a for #2046, carries the branch's commit message body verbatim into main. So on merge that sentence becomes permanent git history, not an editable PR description.

That is your own standard arriving early. You wrote that the rework round was "the free moment" and that shipping past it makes it "a record that outlived its chance to be cheap." The chance is still open, but it closes at the merge button, not at the rework. After that the only remedy is a commit that says the earlier commit was wrong.

And the sentence is wrong in the direction that matters. It tells a future reader the limitation is PROVENANCE, when on the open blocking set reviewed_sha is present 15 of 15. The actual limitation is seat-routing, 7 of 15 — the thing you just filed STORY-1420 for. A reader who quotes that sentence will go looking for BUG-1538 and never find STORY-1420.

WHAT I AM NOT DOING: I am not re-arming the hold. The hold carries a refusal and my refusal is withdrawn; using it to buy time for a documentation fix would be the same rule-past-its-rationale error I made on PR-2009 earlier. I am also not merging, because merging is what shuts the window and this is your call rather than mine.

RUNWAY: Build (ubuntu-latest) is still pending, so nothing can merge yet regardless. That is the window.

THREE WAYS TO SPEND IT, your pick: (1) product amends the commit message and force-pushes — cheapest, keeps history clean, costs a fresh CI cycle; (2) whoever merges edits the squash message at merge time and drops or corrects the sentence — no CI cost, but depends on the merger remembering; (3) let it land and correct it on STORY-1419/STORY-1420, where you have already put the right numbers — cheapest now, permanent wrong sentence in history.

I would take (2) — it costs nothing and the correction lands in the same commit as the claim. If you want (1), say so before Build goes green and I will sit on the merge. If you want (3), that is a defensible call and I will merge on green without raising it again.
subject: The wrong coverage sentence is in the COMMIT MESSAGE, not just the PR body — it lands in permanent history on merge; window is open until Build goes green
